heading: New York Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free New York paycheck calculator to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, New York State income tax, applicable New York City or Yonkers taxes, Social Security, Medicare and employee insurance contributions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and provide your residence and employment information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

New York has several layers of payroll taxation. An employee living in Manhattan may receive a different net paycheck from someone earning the same salary in Albany, Buffalo or elsewhere in New York State.

Understanding these differences can help you evaluate job offers, plan your monthly expenses and make informed financial decisions.

## How to Use the New York Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross compensation before taxes and select your payment frequency.

Enter federal and New York State income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub. Enter applicable NYC or Yonkers withholding separately. Use the annual federal planning option if you want a federal income-tax estimate.

Select whether you are a New York City resident, a Yonkers resident or a nonresident working in Yonkers.

Indicate whether you pay for New York Paid Family Leave and enter prior contributions if you are near the annual cap. Enter disability insurance from your pay stub, along with retirement contributions, healthcare premiums and other applicable deductions.

Review your estimated gross pay, individual deductions and remaining take-home income.

For greater accuracy, use your most recent pay stub and withholding certificates when entering your information.

## How New York State Income Tax Works

New York uses a progressive individual income tax system.

Different portions of taxable income may be subject to different rates. Higher-income employees may also encounter special calculation methods that account for the state's tax benefit recapture provisions.

New York revised its 2026 income tax rate schedules and employer withholding tables to reflect enacted tax rate reductions.

Employers should use [Publication NYS-50-T-NYS](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/publications/withholding/nys50_t_nys.pdf) for the applicable payroll year.

A reliable NYS paycheck calculator must use the authorized withholding methods rather than simply applying annual income tax return brackets to gross salary.

Visit the official [New York withholding tax rate changes page](https://www.tax.ny.gov/bus/wt/rates.htm) for information about the 2026 updates.

## Understanding New York Form IT-2104

New York employees generally use Form IT-2104 to communicate state and applicable local withholding information to employers.

The form allows employees to report withholding allowances and request additional amounts for New York State, New York City and Yonkers taxes.

These state and local withholding elections are separate from the modern federal Form W-4.

Employees may need to complete Form IT-2104.1 when their employment involves nonresident withholding or income allocation.

Review your withholding information if you move, change jobs or experience a significant change in household income.

The [New York withholding forms directory](https://www.tax.ny.gov/forms/withholding_cur_forms.htm) provides official certificates and employer calculation publications.

## New York City Paycheck Calculator

New York City residents generally pay city personal income tax in addition to New York State and federal income taxes.

The ordinary annual NYC personal income tax rates range from 3.078% to 3.876%, depending on taxable income and filing status.

However, actual payroll withholding follows the city's separate employer withholding schedules.

Living in Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, the Bronx or Staten Island may therefore affect your take-home pay compared with living outside New York City.

Employees who commute into New York City from outside the city generally do not pay ordinary NYC resident income tax solely because they work there. Special arrangements can apply to certain city government employees.

Confirm your residence and applicable employment circumstances before selecting NYC withholding.

## Yonkers Resident and Nonresident Taxes

Yonkers has its own local income tax arrangements.

Residents are generally subject to a city income tax surcharge tied to the applicable New York State tax calculation.

Nonresidents performing qualifying employment duties in Yonkers may be subject to a separate earnings tax.

The ordinary Yonkers resident surcharge is 16.75%, while the nonresident earnings tax rate is 0.5%.

The resident surcharge should not be calculated as 16.75% of gross salary. It is associated with the applicable state income tax calculation and must follow the official Yonkers withholding methodology.

Use [Publication NYS-50-T-Y](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/publications/withholding/nys50_t_y.pdf) from the New York Department of Taxation and Finance to determine the appropriate withholding amount.

## New York Paid Family Leave Contributions

New York Paid Family Leave provides financial benefits to eligible workers taking leave for qualifying family-related circumstances.

For 2026, covered employees generally contribute 0.432% of gross covered wages, up to an annual maximum contribution of $411.91.

Visit the official [New York Paid Family Leave website](https://paidfamilyleave.ny.gov/) for current program information.

### Paid Family Leave annual cap example

Suppose you have already contributed $405 toward Paid Family Leave during 2026.

Your next paycheck contains $2,500 in covered wages, ordinarily producing a $10.80 contribution.

However, only $6.91 remains before reaching the annual maximum of $411.91.

Your remaining contribution would therefore be limited to $6.91 under ordinary covered employment.

## New York Disability Insurance Contributions

New York employers may collect employee contributions toward statutory disability benefits coverage.

Under standard arrangements, the employee contribution is limited to 0.5% of weekly wages, with a maximum of $0.60 per week.

For example, an employee earning $1,000 weekly would have a wage-based calculation of $5. However, the standard weekly ceiling limits the contribution to $0.60.

Employers are not required to deduct the contribution from employees and may pay the full cost themselves.

Certain approved enhanced benefit plans can have different contribution arrangements.

Read the official [New York Workers' Compensation Board disability benefits guidance](https://apps.wcb.ny.gov/content/main/DisabilityBenefits/employee-disability-benefits.jsp) for additional information.

## New York Paycheck Example: $78,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $78,000 annually and receiving 26 biweekly paychecks.

Assume the employee is covered by ordinary federal payroll contributions, pays the standard Paid Family Leave contribution and pays the maximum standard disability insurance deduction for two covered weeks.

Approximately $2,756.34 remains before federal income tax, New York State income tax, applicable local taxes and other employee deductions.

This example assumes the employee has not reached any annual contribution limits.

Enter your actual withholding information and residence circumstances to calculate your estimated net paycheck.

## New York Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Suppose you earn $30 per hour and work 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings: $30 × 40 = $1,200.

Overtime earnings: $30 × 1.5 × 6 = $270.

Total gross earnings: $1,470.

Applicable income taxes, payroll contributions and employee benefit deductions are then calculated using their respective taxable wage amounts.

Consult the [New York Department of Labor](https://dol.ny.gov/) for state wage and overtime requirements.

## Comparing New York Salaries and Living Expenses

A salary increase does not necessarily produce an equivalent improvement in disposable income.

Compare your estimated take-home pay alongside housing, transportation, healthcare premiums and employer retirement matching.

Employees considering a move between New York City and another part of New York State should also account for potential differences in local income tax.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Do all New York employees pay NYC income tax?

No. Ordinary New York City personal income tax generally applies to city residents. Nonresidents working in the city do not automatically become subject to the ordinary resident tax.

### How much is New York Paid Family Leave in 2026?

The standard employee contribution is 0.432% of covered gross wages, up to a maximum annual contribution of $411.91.

### Why does my New York paycheck differ from another employee earning the same salary?

Differences in city residency, withholding allowances, healthcare premiums, retirement contributions and year-to-date payroll contributions can affect take-home pay.
